name: David Higgins
story: David Higgins helped locate traditional place names as a member of Kā Huru Manu’s early paepae, documented in Ngāi Tahu’s 2018 project account.
Kā Huru Manu’s early paepae included Trevor Howse, Kelly Davis, Matapura Ellison, Jimmy Russell and David Higgins, while Muriel Johnstone contributed knowledge of the Ōraka Aparima takiwā.

His early work with Matapura Ellison in DOC's Kaupapa Atawhai programme helped explain the need to document historical and cultural information when Papatipu Rūnaka considered South Island high-country pastoral leases. Higgins was one of the first kaumātua paepae guiding the mapping work, which combined archival evidence, iwi-held knowledge and visits to the landscape. The project initially used large topographic map sheets and spreadsheets before adopting connected digital systems.
